\section{Method}
\label{sec:method}

\paragraph{The measured configuration space.}
The real-LLM arm uses Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct on a pool of $N=1500$ MMLU-Pro test items drawn uniformly at random (no length cap).
The declared space has $K=128$ configurations, the product of four demonstration sets (none, or one of three sets of three fixed demonstrations), two option labellings, eight instruction wordings and two answer cues.
A configuration is scored by one forward pass: the model's answer is the option whose letter has the highest log-probability after the cue, and an item is correct if that letter is the gold one; there is no sampling and no generated reasoning.
The $1500\times128$ correctness matrix is computed once and every search, report and verification below is a replay on it.
Demonstration items are not pool items, so they never enter $S$ or the truth.
The default (untuned) configuration is no demonstrations, ``dot'' labelling, the first wording (``Choose the correct option.'') and the cue ``The answer is (''; it was fixed before the matrix was analysed.

\paragraph{Truth and uncertainty.}
For a draw $S$ the truth of the selected configuration is its accuracy on the pool items outside $S$ ($N-n\ge1100$ items, standard error $\le0.015$, of the order of the gaps we measure); every gap is shown beside this floor.
Two sources of uncertainty are kept apart.
The spread of the gap over draws of $S$ is reported as such.
Because draws of $S$ from one pool overlap, the number of draws buys precision only on the gap \emph{for this pool}; every statement about behaviour on the benchmark therefore uses a between-pool interval, from 200 bootstrap resamples of the pool items (200 draws of $S$ each; 2000 on the original pool), with the Monte-Carlo variance of the draws subtracted from the replicate spread.
In a resample a repeated copy of a search item is not a fresh item and is excluded from the truth.
On the synthetic arm $\theta$ is known exactly.

\paragraph{Searchers.}
\emph{Random search} evaluates $B$ configurations drawn without replacement on all of $S$ and returns the best (ties broken at random); $B=K$ is the exhaustive grid.
\emph{Hill climbing} is coordinate ascent over the four factors from a random start, stopping when a full sweep changes nothing.
\emph{Successive halving} scores all candidates on a small random subset of $S$, keeps the best half, and doubles the subset each round, the last round using all of $S$; a floor on the smallest subset matches its evaluation count (configuration--item cells) to that of random search at a given $B$.
The cost of every searcher is counted in cells, so the comparison is at equal evaluation budget.

\paragraph{Predicting the gap from the search log.}
Let $Y_S\in\{0,1\}^{n\times B}$ be the logged item-level scores, $\bar\sigma/\sqrt n$ the mean standard error of a column, and $Z^*\sim\mathcal N(0,\hat\Sigma/n)$ drawn by Gaussian multiplier bootstrap from the centred columns of $Y_S$ \citep{chernozhukov2013}.
If all configurations had the same accuracy the expected optimism of the best one is $\EE\max_k Z^*_k=\kappa\,\bar\sigma/\sqrt n$, which defines $\kappa$ and is the first predictor.
The refined predictor shrinks the $S$-scores toward their mean by $\hat\sigma_\theta^2/(\hat\sigma_\theta^2+\mathrm{se}_k^2)$, with $\hat\sigma_\theta^2$ the spread of the scores minus the mean noise variance, adds $Z^*$, selects the maximiser $k^*$ and returns $\EE Z^*_{k^*}$.
$\Keff$ is the number of independent standard-normal competitors whose expected maximum equals $\kappa$ (Blom's approximation).

shown.message:
I applied `experiment-repo`'s corrections to the Method section and pushed them to `dev`. The paper builds locally. No version is offered yet.

- **Pool size:** the Method now gives the number of fresh items per experiment, at least 1100 for n ≤ 400 and at least 1260 in the protocol runs.
- **Gap against the pool outside S:** I added the 1.36 factor at n = 400, so a reader can tell which reading a point is.
- **Candidate sets:** the Method now defines the evaluated set for each searcher. For successive halving it is the two configurations that reach the last round, and only the declared set is valid there.
- **Max-t:** the width factor is the binomial standard error, and the multiplier bootstrap uses 500 draws.
- **Šidák:** it is reported next to Bonferroni. The unadjusted bound on the selected configuration is named as the reference.
- **Scoring:** the paired scoring is described, and the synthetic arm has one exact scoring.
- **Decision tests:** they are described as the paired z-test (z > 1.645) and the simultaneous and split versions.
- **Resample counts:** I removed the fixed "200 resamples" from the Method. Each result will give its own count, since `experiment-repo` says the real protocol and decision runs will use a smaller number set by remaining compute.

The delivered result files and the real-matrix runs don't exist yet; the matrix is about 5 of 504 blocks done. The experiments section, the semi-synthetic and leakage Method text, the abstract and the introduction all wait on those results. I told `experiment-repo` in #5 that the corrections are in.
